messages.author: e3f6ab3a7788d4ea
messages.subject: Model fits not as expected
parts:
Hi Chris,

I have GPS data for cockatoos for which I am trying to calculate home ranges.

I'm having trouble producing a model with a good fit to my variograms.  After saving model parameters to GUESS and plotting the expected model fit, the fits look great. However after running the model using the saved GUESS parameters, the fit looks nothing like expected.

Having read a few threads on here with similar issues, I wonder if it is something to do with the errors.  I don't have calibration data for my tags but I do have a GPS.HDOP column. When I set the GUESS parameters I add in an estimate for errors (20m is what I have been using - the published error for our tags).  Is this all I need to do in order for the model incorporate my GPS.HDOP column and account for the errors?  The summary outputs include an error estimate so I know the error is being incorporated but I'm wondering if there's something more I should be doing.

Also our data interval is inconsistent - 2.5 minutes during the day (15 minutes during periods of low solar recharge) and dropping to 30 minutes at night. I'm wondering if this having an impact on the model.

Thanks in advance for your help,

Karen

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Model fits not as expected
parts:
Hi Karen,

I would recommend updated to the development version of the package on GitHub [via devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm") ] and calculating the variograms with error=TRUE.

If you don't have calibration data, I would recommend a credible prior: https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/error.html#model-fitting-1
If the posterior error estimates come out substantially different from the prior, then you can re-calibrate the data based on that and recalculate the variogram (with error=TRUE again) to see if it matches better. There is some functionality I can add to make that easier if it might be useful.

20 meters is for errors at HDOP=1 or over the average? It makes a difference in the model. 20 meters at HDOP=1 is a little high but not implausible. You might check if your device is listed in the appendix of https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.06.12.130195v1

All else being equal, irregular sampling is fine with continuous-time methods. That is their main advantage.

Best,
Chris
